proponent_claim: Near-continuous orbital solar lowers the energy term.
required_observable: Delivered annual IT kWh, solar degradation, conversion losses, eclipse duty, and achieved compute availability.
current_result: Direction accepted; AI1 nameplate values are disclosed, but achieved availability and full energy cost are not.

proponent_claim: Radiative rejection can reduce cooling-power overhead.
model_term: radiator mass/capex; pumping load; thermal margin
required_observable: Sustained heat rejection, coolant and junction temperatures, full-loop mass, parasitic power, degradation, and failures.
current_result: 110 m² is disclosed; full thermal performance, mass, power, cost, and life are not.

required_observable: Achieved reusable payload, fully allocated cost/kg, turnaround, fleet size, reliability, and licensed cadence.
current_result: $185/kg is a target-derived ceiling; the SEC response says launch asset depreciation remains part of satellite cost.

proponent_claim: Scaled satellite manufacturing lowers spacecraft cost.
required_observable: Recurring factory cost per delivered kW, yield, throughput, NRE allocation, and acceptance-test cost.
current_result: Factory scale is stated; no comparable manufacturing cost or yield is disclosed.

required_observable: As-flown mass divided by sustained average delivered IT kW at equal service quality.
current_result: AI1 states 70 kW/t and the long-run filing uses 100 kW/t; an independent conventional study gives 34–59 kg/kW.

proponent_claim: Proprietary chips reduce hardware cost and depreciation.
model_term: qualified hardware capex; refresh life; efficiency
required_observable: Qualified accelerator cost, useful FLOP/s or accepted tokens per watt, yield, failure rate, and economic refresh life.
current_result: Compute depreciation is identified as the largest component; no comparable value or achieved chip trajectory is disclosed.

proponent_claim: Orbital hardware remains useful long enough to amortize.
required_observable: Cohort survival, radiation faults, degradation, repair, and economic retirement under the fixed workload.
current_result: AI1 life is not disclosed; seven years in the hybrid is an ASSUMPTION.

proponent_claim: Laser and Starlink links deliver useful output globally.
required_observable: Sustained application goodput, latency distribution, contention, outages, gateway capacity, and cost.
current_result: Link architecture is described; delivered application goodput and cost are not.

proponent_claim: Replacement and modular upgrades preserve value.
required_observable: Demonstrated payload exchange or repair, replacement mass/cadence, downtime, and recovered value.
current_result: Modularity is stated; no orbital repair, exchange, or AI1 replacement record is disclosed.

proponent_claim: Orbit reaches useful power faster than terrestrial projects.
model_term: production, launch, commissioning, and constellation ramp
required_observable: Contract-to-service dates and accepted-output ramp for matched orbital and terrestrial deployments.
current_result: Possible initial deployment is stated for 2028; commissioning and useful-output ramp are missing.

proponent_claim: Terrestrial power scarcity widens the orbital advantage.
model_term: Earth power price, PUE, interconnection and construction schedule
required_observable: Matched forward power, cooling, site, interconnection, construction, and financing trajectories.
current_result: The generic model tests tight/base/responsive Earth cases; SpaceX supplies no matched escalation path.

proponent_claim: Space becomes the lowest-cost place for AI by January 2028–January 2029.
model_term: full LCO and accepted-output cost ratios plus schedule
required_observable: A frozen comparator, workload, quality boundary, full lifecycle bill, and commissioned accepted output by each deadline.
current_result: Company-only comparison is not computable; the registered hybrid remains above Earth on both steady-state denominators.
